![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/3f27cf1fddfbbbdb9dd2593567743494ae15e061bca8d1e111ac1f1561561943.png)

Consider the finite region above bounded by $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=\sqrt{x},$ as shown above. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{2}$ and $g(x)=\sqrt{x}.$

First, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ {x}^{2} & =\sqrt{x} \\ {x}^{2}-\sqrt{x} & =0 \\ \sqrt{x}({x}^{3/2}-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=1.$

Let's draw our vertical arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing *away* from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/bf8d9039cbaa7fe5559d8d9d036063739e572b2abc46741668a88c09d9bcd28a.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $y=f(x)={x}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $y=g(x)=\sqrt{x}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({[\sqrt{x}]}^{2}-{[{x}^{2}]}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}(x-{x}^{4})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\pi [(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{5})-0] \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
